title: Benchmark-Driven Development Process
purpose: Establish a repeatable process for using benchmarks to validate changes, detect regressions, and drive optimization decisions. Based on the repository's empirical benchmark infrastructure (tool_benchmarker.py, tool_tester.py, coord_stress_bench.py) which has produced 3,247 data points across 17 sources and validated 45 tool tests with zero failures.
scope: All changes to coordination infrastructure, tools, scripts, and communication primitives. Applies to any code that could affect latency, throughput, correctness, or token efficiency.

data_gathering_iteration_gains.lesson: Second iteration of benchmarks always shows massive gains. Always iterate.

procedures.title: Run Baseline Benchmarks Before Changes
procedures.action: Before making any changes to coordination or tool code, run the relevant benchmark suite to establish a baseline.

tool_regression.baseline_metric: All 45 tests pass, individual tool timings recorded

coordination_benchmarks.what_it_tests: Hub operations, help protocol, channels, work stealing, pipelines, SQLite contention, team size scaling
coordination_benchmarks.baseline_metric: ops/sec and p95/p99 latency for each category

token_efficiency.what_it_tests: Token consumption for query_kb, smart_read, smart_write operations
token_efficiency.baseline_metric: Token count and savings percentage per operation

data_gathering.what_it_tests: All data-gathering methods (WebSearch, Wikipedia, arXiv, Hybrid, Iterative, OpenAlex, Wikidata)
data_gathering.baseline_metric: Speed, data points collected, quality score per method

procedures.output: Baseline benchmark results saved to storage/scripts/ with timestamp

procedures.title: Make Changes with Regression Awareness
procedures.action: Implement changes. For each modified file, identify which benchmark suite covers it.
procedures.output: List of benchmark suites to re-run after changes

procedures.title: Run Post-Change Benchmarks
procedures.action: After changes, re-run all relevant benchmark suites. Compare against baseline.
procedures.comparison_method: For each metric, compute the ratio: (post_change / baseline). Flag any metric that exceeds regression thresholds.
procedures.output: Post-change benchmark results with comparison to baseline

procedures.title: Apply Regression Detection Thresholds
procedures.action: Check all metrics against regression thresholds. Any threshold breach requires investigation before the change is accepted.

correctness.threshold: Any test failure is a blocking regression
correctness.action: Fix before proceeding. Zero tolerance for correctness regressions.

latency_p95.action: Investigate cause. If inherent to the change (e.g., added safety check), document and accept. If unintended, fix.
latency_p95.example: Hub status update p95 increases from 0.485ms to 0.600ms (24% increase) -> investigate

throughput.action: Investigate. Throughput regressions compound across many operations.
throughput.example: SQLite ops/sec drops from 3611 to 3000 (17% decrease) -> investigate

token_efficiency.action: Investigate. Token regressions directly reduce agent context window budget.
token_efficiency.example: query_kb tokens increase from 123 to 140 (14% increase) -> investigate

memory.action: Investigate. Memory increases can affect stability at scale.
memory.example: query_kb peak memory increases from 14.8MB to 23MB (55% increase) -> investigate

procedures.output: Regression report: pass/fail per threshold with investigation notes

procedures.title: Store Benchmark Results
procedures.action: Save all benchmark results (baseline and post-change) for historical tracking.

storage_format.location: storage/scripts/ (for tool and coordination benchmarks), storage/scripts/data-gathering/benchmarks/ (for data gathering)
storage_format.retention: Keep all results. They form the historical trend used to detect gradual regressions.

procedures.title: Update Baselines After Accepted Changes
procedures.action: After a change passes regression checks and is accepted, update the canonical baseline values in this SOP and any monitoring dashboards.
baseline_update_rules: Only update baselines after verified successful changes
Keep the previous baseline as a reference point
If a regression was accepted (documented and justified), note the new baseline with the justification
Never update baselines silently - always log the change and reason

always_before_and_after: Changes to any coordination module (coordinator_hub.py, help_protocol.py, direct_channels.py, work_stealing.py)
Changes to any tool in storage/scripts/ that is covered by tool_tester.py
Changes to SQLite access patterns or WAL configuration
Changes to bus file I/O (bus_cli.py, message serialization)
before_after_recommended: Changes to knowledge base read/write tools
New tool additions (add to tool_tester.py first)
periodic_no_change_needed: Weekly: Run full tool regression suite to catch environmental regressions
Per operation: Run coordination benchmarks before multi-agent deployment to validate infrastructure health
Per data-gathering session: Run method benchmarks to track external API availability and performance

anti_patterns.name: Ship Without Benchmarking
anti_patterns.description: Making changes to coordination or tool code without running benchmarks.
anti_patterns.why_wrong: Silent regressions accumulate. A 5% throughput regression per change compounds to 40% loss after 10 changes.
anti_patterns.fix: Always run relevant benchmark suite before and after changes.

anti_patterns.name: Benchmark Only p50
anti_patterns.description: Checking only mean or median latency and declaring success.
anti_patterns.why_wrong: p50 stays constant at ~0.24ms for SQLite regardless of contention. The real regressions show in p95/p99 tail latency.
anti_patterns.fix: Always check p95 and p99 in addition to median.

anti_patterns.name: One-Shot Benchmarking
anti_patterns.description: Running benchmarks once during initial development but never again.
anti_patterns.why_wrong: Data-gathering iteration 1 to 2 showed 371% improvement. First benchmarks establish a baseline; subsequent iterations validate and improve.
anti_patterns.fix: Iterate on benchmarks. Run them regularly. Track trends over time.

anti_patterns.name: Ignoring Token Regression
anti_patterns.description: Treating token consumption as unimportant because the operation still works.
anti_patterns.why_wrong: 90.2% token reduction enables 11.7x more operations per context window. A 10% token regression means agents fit 10% fewer operations, compounding across every agent in every session.
anti_patterns.fix: Track token consumption as a first-class metric alongside latency and throughput.

references.data_points: 45 tests across 12 tools, query_kb and smart_read benchmarks
2 iterations of method benchmarks showing 371% improvement
Token efficiency and iteration improvement insights

compliance_indicators: Baseline benchmarks run before every infrastructure change
Post-change benchmarks run and compared against baseline
Regression thresholds checked: correctness (0 tolerance), latency p95 (<20% increase), throughput (<15% decrease), tokens (<10% increase)
metrics.measurement_method: Compare post-change metrics against stored baselines. Flag any metric exceeding regression thresholds. Track trends over time to detect gradual degradation.
